conventions.rule: A state is a circle labelled with its name; an accepting state is a double circle.
conventions.source: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., ch. 1.1

conventions.rule: The start state has an arrow pointing at it from nowhere.
conventions.source: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., ch. 1.1

recipes.rule: Each transition is one arrow labelled with the symbols it reads, separated by commas.
recipes.source: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., ch. 1.1

rules.rule: Exactly one state has the start arrow.
rules.source: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., ch. 1.1

rules.rule: In a DFA every state has exactly one outgoing arrow for each input symbol.
rules.source: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., ch. 1.1

rules.rule: The root is the start variable and the leaves, read left to right, spell the derived string.
rules.source: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed., ch. 2.1

test_page.content:
A DFA over {0, 1} that accepts strings with an even number of 0s: states q0 (start, accepting) and q1;
0 moves between q0 and q1, 1 loops on each state.
